doc.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Double bass drums and the great drummers
title: Ray McKinley and who was first with two bass drums
summary: McKinley told him that Bellson was the first, with McKinley playing two bass drums by mallets in Double Drum Boogie; Bellson believes he was first to add pedals.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: A lot of people point to Ray McKinley using double bass drums. It sounds like you preceded him at least as far as the idea.

I thought he was the first one, but later on he told me, “No. It was you. You were the first one.” He came up – he was with Will Bradley’s band. Double Drum Boogie came up with him. He had two bass drums, and he played them with mallets. I thought – I kept giving people the idea that Ray was the first one. When I finally saw him, he said, “No. You were the first one, Lou.” I said, “You’re older than I am, so I figured [it was] from you.”
Did he actually have two pedals on it, or was he just using the bass drums and playing them with his hands.
That I don’t know. I’m inclined to think he was just using the mallets. Then later on, I think, when he saw me he added the pedals.
But you were the first one that you know of to actually affix pedals to bass drums and play them.
So we can set the record straight now.
No, it might have been some guy living in a cave 300 years ago. I don’t know.
Until that information comes out, right now we’ll go with what we got, which is Louie Bellson coming up with that design in 1938, from a design.
